Parent

Center

• Add and edit activities: details, ages, days and times, price, group size, staff, photos.

• See an overview of its activities and requests.

## Shopify Expert Needed – Technical Fixes, Speed Optimization, SEO, AEO/GEO & Conversion Improvement

**About the Business**

Sherryi Baby Care (www\.sherryi\.com) is a US\-based baby care brand selling breast milk storage products through Shopify\.

We are looking for an experienced Shopify developer with strong technical SEO expertise to improve our existing store’s performance, search visibility, and customer shopping experience\.

Our primary goal is to fix existing issues, increase qualified organic traffic, and improve conversions — not simply redesign the website\.

**1\. Shopify Technical Fixes**

- Identify and repair broken links, including social media links\.
- Check navigation, product availability, and Add to Cart functionality\.
- Investigate inconsistent product ratings and review displays\.
- Resolve identified storefront errors\.
- Ensure a smooth mobile and desktop shopping experience\.

- Identify and address slow mobile loading and Core Web Vitals issues\.
- Optimize images without compromising product image quality\.
- Review unnecessary scripts, apps, and theme\-related performance issues\.
- Improve loading behavior and mobile responsiveness\.

- Review and correct indexing and crawlability issues\.
- Optimize page titles, meta descriptions, canonical URLs, and internal linking\.
- Review sitemap and robots\.txt configurations\.

- Identify and address technical SEO errors\.

**4\. AI Search Optimization (AEO/GEO)**

- Improve content structure to support discoverability through AI\-powered search experiences, including ChatGPT, Gemini, and Google AI\.
- Optimize relevant product descriptions, headings, and FAQs\.
- Improve structured product information and relevant schema markup\.
- Recommend practical, evidence\-based AI search optimization improvements\.

We understand that rankings, AI citations, and organic sales cannot be guaranteed\.

**5\. Conversion Rate Optimization**

- Improve product page clarity, trust signals, and calls to action\.
- Identify usability issues that may prevent customers from purchasing\.
- Recommend and implement agreed improvements to the shopping journey\.

### Design Requirements

We are not automatically requesting a complete website redesign\.

Please review the existing store and explain whether targeted improvements would be more cost\-effective\.

If you recommend a redesign, provide a separate quote and explain its expected benefits\.

### Deliverables

- Implemented fixes, not just recommendations\.
- Before\-and\-after performance measurements\.

- Testing of key storefront functionality\.
- Work on a duplicate Shopify theme where applicable, with approval before publishing\.

leads.title: Machine Learning Engineer — One Seat on a Small Team That Gets Sent In
leads.desc:
Every large company has a standing army of engineers: thousands of people, each owning one narrow slice, moving at the speed of the slowest approval.

This is the other thing. The small team that gets sent in when the standing army can’t solve it.

We’re a small, senior engineering unit with a standing mandate across a growing family of companies in a range of industries. When one of them hits a problem its own people can’t crack (a process drowning in manual work, a model nobody trusts, a question of whether machine learning belongs there at all), we get sent in. There are more problems waiting than people to send. That’s why this seat is open.

We add one person at a time, and we take our time choosing. We’d rather leave a seat empty than fill it wrong. One seat is open now, for a machine learning engineer.

THE WORK
You’ll be dropped into a company you’ve never seen. The data will be uncleaned, the process half-documented, and the people who’ve done the job by hand for years will know things that aren’t written down anywhere. Your assignment arrives as an objective, not a spec:

“This workflow runs on manual classification. Find out whether we can automate it, and prove it.”
“The model they’re using gives inconsistent answers. Find out why. Tell us what to change.”
“Someone thinks there’s an ML opportunity in this process. Find out whether they’re right.”

You learn the terrain fast. You interrogate the data and sit with the operators. You set a baseline and define what “good” means before you build anything. Then you choose the tool: an LLM, gradient boosting, a retrieval system, or 200 lines of deterministic code. And you’ll have the standing to say “don’t build this” when that’s the right answer.

What you ship has to keep working after we’ve moved on. Tests, monitoring, rollback, documentation. A business will be running on it.

IT WILL BE HARD
The data will be worse than you expect. Requirements will shift after you’ve started. You’ll spend three weeks on an approach, learn it’s wrong, and the right move will be to throw it out without flinching. The person you most need to talk to will be too busy. And you’ll be judged on whether the thing works, not on how hard you tried.

If that paragraph made you lean in rather than back, keep reading.

WHY THIS AND NOT THE BIG-COMPANY JOB
At a large company you own a metric. Your model is one of four hundred. You’ll spend a quarter in launch review, never meet the person whose job your work changed, and watch your best idea die in a planning doc.

Here, you are the machine learning capability. What you decide is what gets built. You’ll see more real ML problems in two years than most engineers see in ten: different industries, different data, different ways things break. You’ll learn how businesses actually make money, from inside them, alongside the people who own them and make the calls. And your work will go into production at companies that run on it. The people who run them will know your name.

We track acknowledgements, follow-ups and settlement progress.

The form submitter and the affected customer may be different people. One customer may also have multiple claims. Contacts, cases, documents and communications must therefore be correctly linked.

1. Automated intake and case creation

Assign a case owner and create initial tasks.

Our existing Excel tracker contains insurer details, claim references, incident dates, customer contact information, investigation status, document request and receipt dates, reminders, insurer acknowledgements, handover and closure dates, communication milestones, compensation, financial administration, notes and time spent.

Excellent attention to detail.

Verified: WhatsApp number is explicitly published by an official hotel source.

Today: the day’s task list
Now: the current task, with a large START button
How: one step at a time, each with a short sentence, a photo and “Step X of Y”, plus BACK and NEXT
Check: a short checklist the student ticks after physically checking the work
Done: a prompt to report to staff, with a suggested phrase
Next: the next scheduled task

An “I need help” button stays visible on every screen.

Staff section (PIN-protected)

Create, edit, duplicate and archive task templates
Add steps, photos and checklists, and reorder steps
Set up help phrases and completion phrases
Schedule and order the day’s tasks

Runs in the browser on iPad (other tablets are a plus) and works offline
No recurring hosting or subscription needed for normal use
Large touch targets, a minimal UI and protection against accidentally leaving the active task
Nothing employer-specific is hard-coded; everything is configured through templates
Full source code and IP handed over on completion
Confidential project: no reuse of project content in your portfolio without approval

leads.title: Software architect with hands on Mastra.ai experience
leads.desc:
Looking for an architect/consultant with hands-on Mastra experience to help design an AI assistant embedded in a CRM and booking system.

Stack: Next.js, Supabase/Postgres, Railway.

The assistant should behave like a junior administrator across an ongoing customer/booking lifecycle:

Work across emails, internal notes, call transcripts, documents and current CRM records.
Investigate a situation using tools, then prepare related updates, draft replies, documents and follow-ups for human review.
Handle multiple email conversations about the same booking, with different participants and topics.
Stay aware of changes made directly by staff or customers in the application.
Continue unfinished work across later messages, approvals and long histories.
Email is one channel. Staff might also leave an internal instruction, mention the assistant in a note, or change a booking status.

Example: A customer requests a discount by email. A manager approves it in an internal note. The assistant should connect that decision to the original request, check the current booking and pricing, and prepare the appropriate updates and customer reply. Meanwhile, another conversation concerns booking details. If those details change before someone approves the draft, the assistant needs to account for that.

We’d like help choosing a practical architecture for:

Thread/session boundaries and shared customer/booking context.
Current application state versus conversation memory and retrieved evidence.
Wake-up rules, batching routine edits and continuing pending work.
Human approval, retries and avoiding duplicate actions.
Which Mastra facilities to use and what should remain application code.
The aim is a maintainable implementation with as few moving parts as reasonably possible.

leads.title: Python + ffmpeg tool: cut a long video into captioned vertical Shorts
leads.desc:
We make YouTube videos with an automated pipeline (Python, ffmpeg, AI voice and avatar tools). We need one more step built as a small standalone command line tool. This is a small fixed price job, paid through Upwork. Please don't start the work or send samples before you're hired. We pay for everything you build.

WHAT THE TOOL DOES

Inputs:
1. A long 16:9 MP4, 10 to 60 minutes.
2. A JSON file listing the clips to cut. Each clip has a name, a start time and an end time, for example: name clip01, start 00:01:05.200, end 00:01:48.000.
3. Optional: an SRT captions file for the whole long video.

For each clip it writes:
1. A 1080x1920 MP4 (H.264 video, AAC audio) at the source frame rate, with frame accurate cuts.
2. Framing set by an option: "crop" (center crop, with an optional left or right offset) or "fill" (the whole 16:9 frame in the middle, with a blurred, enlarged copy of it behind).
3. If an SRT was given: the captions for that clip's time range, retimed to the clip and burned in. White text with a black outline in the lower third. Font file, size and position set by options. A caption line that crosses the clip's start or end is trimmed to fit, not dropped.
4. Audio normalized to an integrated loudness of minus 14 LUFS.
5. A JPG contact sheet of 6 evenly spaced frames, so we can check the clip at a glance.

REQUIREMENTS
1. Runs on macOS (Apple Silicon) with Python 3.11 or newer and ffmpeg from Homebrew. No paid services, no cloud, no GPU.
2. One command runs everything. Each setting above can be changed with a command line option.
3. Clear error messages when a file is missing or a clip's times fall outside the video. One bad clip shouldn't stop the others.
4. A README with install steps, one example run and every option explained.
5. Test it on any Creative Commons video, for example Blender's open movie Big Buck Bunny. We'll also test it on our own footage.
6. AI coding tools are fine. You're responsible for the code working.

NOT INCLUDED: transcription (we already have captions), face tracking, uploading.

DONE WHEN: we run your example command on our Mac and on one of our own videos, and every clip comes out at the right size and length, with the captions in sync and no manual fixes. One round of fixes is included.

TIMELINE: please deliver within 5 days of being hired.

PAYMENT: one fixed price milestone, funded when you're hired and released when the test above passes. We review within 2 business days of delivery.

If this goes well we may have more pipeline work, but we can't promise it.

Access control is the core of the product:
    •    Buyers in the same deal must never see each other's documents, requests, questions, answers or identity.
    •    The bank's internal files, notes and draft answers must never reach the seller, the buyers or observers.
    •    Each deal has several roles (advisor, seller, buyers, observers) with different permissions.
The product also has AI features: document search, chat, and drafted answers to diligence requests. It is running in production with test data and has no paying customers yet.
Why this role exists:
The platform was built by a very small team with use of AI coding agents. It has a large automated test suite and has been through several internal security audits. What it has not had is an experienced engineer reading it end to end with fresh eyes. That is this job.


Project Overview
   •    Category: Web, Mobile & Software Dev & Back-End Development
    •    Project type: One-time project with follow-on milestones, 1 freelancer
    •    Length: 1 to 2 months
    •    Experience level: Expert
    •    Location: Worldwide. Europe and Asia welcome.
    •    Skills: Golang, Software Architecture, Code Review, Web Application Security, SQLite, Amazon Web Services, API Development


The stack
    •    One Go service (chi router): about 65,000 lines, plus roughly 200 test files
    •    SQLite, one database per firm and per deal
    •    Encrypted documents in S3
    •    Server-rendered HTML templates with plain JavaScript, no SPA framework
    •    One AWS EC2 host (arm64), Caddy, SES, Paddle billing, OIDC SSO, TOTP MFA
    •    LLM and embeddings through a hosted inference API
    •    Three web apps: sign-in, firm workspace, per-deal room


What you will do:
Phase 1, fixed price, two weeks. Read the code and the docs, run it, and give us a written assessment covering:
    •    Architecture and operational risk
    •    Authorization and tenant isolation, including whether one buyer can see another buyer's requests, questions or documents, and whether the bank's internal files stay internal
    •    General security: secrets handling, encryption and key management, logging, backups, and the gaps a bank's or CPA firm's vendor-security review would raise
    •    Code quality and maintainability

leads.title: Multi-Tenant Voice AI Receptionist Engine
leads.desc:
Project Goal
To build a scalable, low-latency, multi-tenant Voice AI receptionist system tailored for local home-service businesses (starting with plumbers). The architecture must completely bypass premium orchestration wrappers (like Vapi/Retell) to achieve a target operating cost of $0.03 to $0.04 USD per minute using an open-source pipeline.
2. Required Core Architecture
You are required to build and stitch the pipeline using the following open-source and wholesale infrastructure components:
• Telephony Carrier: Telnyx (preferred for lower latency) or Twilio.
• Orchestration Framework: LiveKit Agents (Python or TypeScript) or Pipecat.
• Speech-to-Text (STT): Deepgram Nova-2 via streaming WebSockets.
• Large Language Model (LLM): OpenAI GPT-4o-mini or Groq Llama-3.1-70B.
• Text-to-Speech (TTS): Cartesia (Sonic) or Deepgram Aura.
3. Key Feature Requirements
• Dynamic Multi-Tenancy: The backend engine must handle calls for multiple independent plumbing businesses simultaneously. When a call hits the telephony webhook, the system must read the incoming dialed number (to_number), look it up in a central database, and dynamically inject that specific business's Company Name, Operating Rules, and Instruction Prompt into the LLM context.
• Conversational Logic: The AI must politely greet callers, collect their name, phone number, and a description of their plumbing issue. If an active flood/emergency is mentioned, it must provide immediate safety instructions (e.g., “Please turn off your main water valve immediately while I notify our technician”).
• End-of-Call Webhook (Data Routing): Within 30 seconds of a call hanging up, the system must trigger an outbound JSON payload/webhook containing the full call transcript, an AI-generated 2-sentence summary, and the extracted customer contact details.
4. Out of Scope (What you do NOT need to build)
• You do not need to build a custom frontend user dashboard for clients.
• You do not need to build complex custom text-messaging features; we will be using a simple webhook connected to Make.com to handle the post-call routing to Google Sheets and SMS.
5. Hosting & Deployment
• The final production-ready code repository must be securely deployed onto a scalable, low-cost cloud provider (Railway, DigitalOcean, or AWS) using a Docker container or equivalent configuration.
• All environment variables must point to API accounts owned and funded by me.

Next Steps to Send with This:

You will help ensure the solution is well-structured, efficient, and aligned with our goals from the start.

We are two consultancies building a free AI agent that helps nonprofits plan their programs and how they will measure them. It walks users through a three-step planning framework: a theory of change, a logic model, and a logframe (the results table that lists goals, outputs, outcomes, indicators, and assumptions). The pilot focuses on family planning, a field with well-established global indicators and strong professional networks for sourcing and testing. 

The questions we need help with
1.	Extraction from PDFs. What is the best way to use AI to pull usable content out of messy PDFs? Logframes are usually multi-page tables, theories of change are often diagrams, some files are scanned, and terminology varies a lot between organizations. We want a process our analysts can run and repeat.
2.	Whole documents vs. extracted pieces. Our current leaning is to keep whole documents with rich tags, because breaking them apart can lose the logic linking one level to the next. We also need structured data, such as each outcome and the indicators that measure it. How should we balance the two?
3.	Data structure. How should we represent the results chain (impact → outcome → output → activity → indicator) and our tags so the data works for the agent? What should our metadata and rules files look like?
4.	Vector database. We plan to use a vector database (one that lets the agent search by meaning, not just exact words). We need advice on which one, how to structure it, and hands-on help setting it up.
5.	Models, hosting, and cost. Our preference is to build on an existing commercial AI model rather than train our own, likely hosted in Microsoft Azure. We want a sanity check on that and a rough estimate of running costs.

- Play the game often and give the agent specific feedback. “Jumping feels floaty because gravity is too low” is useful. “Make it better” is not.
- Keep going until the game compiles, runs and is fun to play.
- Write up a few of the hard technical problems you hit, using a template and tools we provide, then package and submit the game.

The back-and-forth is what matters most to us: what you notice, how you diagnose it, and how you push the agent toward a fix.

$100 per approved, completed game. Once you’re set up, each game should take no more than a couple of hours to create, and you’ll be able to build several in parallel while the coding agents are running. We can make 1 game for $100 or up to 5 for $500. We may have further contracts in future.

- Hands-on Unreal Engine experience (Blueprints and/or C++), professional or serious hobby.

Clear written communication and the ability to follow a detailed setup guide.

Requirements

- Unreal Engine 5.7, installed through the Epic Games Launcher.
- A Windows 11 PC with 16 GB+ RAM, 8+ CPU threads and 300 GB+ free disk space. An NVIDIA GPU is recommended.
- A paid Claude Code or Codex plan.
- GitHub and Epic Games accounts.
- A stable internet connection that can handle large uploads.

How your work is used

We’re studying how experienced developers build games with AI coding agents, so the build process matters more to us than the finished game. Your direction to the agent, the problems you hit and how you solved them are used to help improve AI coding tools. We don’t release the games as products.

Our tools only log what happens inside your game sessions, and they record in plain text, so you can see exactly what’s captured at any time. We’ll guide you through setup and do a short kickoff call before your first game.

We’re looking for an advertising specialist to review a small set of existing Kaedrin campaigns and help us understand our spending, conversion tracking and next practical improvement.

Kaedrin provides resume and career document services. We use Google Ads, Meta Ads and ChatGPT Ads. This assignment is a focused diagnostic, with the campaigns and reporting period agreed before work begins.

What we need
1. Spending and activity review
Compare reported spending, configured budgets and campaign activity using the records provided. Distinguish advertising spend from billed charges and flag discrepancies or missing information.
2. Conversion tracking diagnosis
Review how clicks connect to genuine inquiries, qualified buyers and payments. Identify where measurement breaks down and recommend the smallest practical fix using our existing systems.
3. One prioritized improvement
Recommend one bounded test. Explain why it deserves priority, its estimated cost, how success would be measured and when we should stop. If the evidence does not justify a campaign test, explain which information or measurement must be established first.
4. Knowledge transfer
Deliver a short written report with supporting evidence, diagnostic steps and reusable instructions. Clearly separate verified findings from assumptions and unanswered questions. We want practical guidance we can understand and use, not a slide deck. You should be comfortable working independently, following written instructions and documenting your reasoning so our team can reuse what you learn.

Scope and access
This is a review only. No ad changes, budget increases, campaign launches, tracking implementation or ongoing management are included.
We will initially provide reports and appropriately redacted exports. Any additional access must be agreed separately. We will not share passwords. Use aggregate purchase information or redacted transaction evidence only. No customer names, resumes, payment credentials or unrestricted customer records.
We understand that incomplete data may prevent a definitive diagnosis. Explain those limits rather than guessing. This engagement does not guarantee further work.

Relevant experience
Please have hands on Google Ads and Meta Ads measurement experience. ChatGPT Ads familiarity is helpful, but be honest about your experience with each platform.

Please answer these questions
1. Describe a case where you investigated a mismatch between reported conversions and actual revenue. What did you find?
2. What would you check first for this assignment?
3. Which advertising platforms and tracking tools have you personally used?
Please confirm that you can complete this bounded review for $150 and state your expected turnaround time.

leads.title: AI Digital Marketing & Growth Specialist – Australian Finance Business
leads.desc:
AI Digital Marketing & Growth Specialist – Australian Finance Business

Part-time | Remote | Nepal preferred | Long-term opportunity**

About Charter Finance

Charter Finance is an established Australian mortgage and finance broking business specialising in residential, commercial, business and property development finance.

We offer considerably more than traditional transactional mortgage broking.

Our approach focuses on helping clients understand how to structure and manage debt, improve their cash flow, build equity and make informed financial decisions over time.

We work with professionals, business owners, property investors, sophisticated borrowers and first-home buyers, as well as professional advisers who refer clients requiring specialist lending expertise.

Our Financial Wholeness philosophy is centred on helping clients understand where they are financially, where they want to go and how their borrowing arrangements and financial habits can support their objectives.

We're looking to expand our digital presence and attract more of the clients who genuinely value this approach.

The role

We're seeking an experienced, proactive **AI Digital Marketing & Growth Specialist** to take ownership of our content execution, social media distribution and digital growth initiatives.

We already have an internal AI content-generation system, developed using Claude.

You'll work alongside our existing team to improve, adapt, publish and maximise the commercial value of that content.

We are not looking for someone who simply copies AI-generated posts into Canva and uploads them to social media. Eg: seeing the word 'quietly' in the content, one knows its not been proof read and comes across as AI slop.

We want someone who can think, research, challenge ideas and proactively identify opportunities to grow our visibility and attract suitable prospective clients.

Your responsibilities

**Social media management and publishing**

- Manage content across LinkedIn, Instagram, FBook, YouTube and Google Business Profile.
- Publish content to both our company accounts and the founder's professional profiles, where appropriate.
- Adapt content to suit each platform's audience and format.
- Develop effective hooks, captions, thumbnails, graphics and calls to action.
- Maintain a consistent publishing calendar and manage approved content.
- Monitor engagement, comments and relevant opportunities for follow-up.

**Video editing and content repurposing**

- Edit videos recorded by our founder.
- Produce Reels, Shorts and LinkedIn videos.
- Add subtitles, captions, graphics and engaging openings.
- Repurpose longer recordings into concise, useful short-form content.
- Maintain a consistent, professional visual identity.

AI-assisted research and content improvement**

- Work with our existing Claude-based content agent.
- Help improve content quality, originality and relevance.
- Research Australian financial news and identify worthwhile content opportunities.
